title: Quiz: Diagnosing and Handling Missing Values

questions.text: In the MCAR mechanism, the probability of a value being missing is:
options: Equal for all records, regardless of any variable in the dataset
Related to the values of other observed variables
Related to the value that is actually missing
Always less than 5% of the dataset
questions.explanation: MCAR (Missing Completely At Random) means the probability of missingness is the same for every record and is not related to any other variable — observed or unobserved. Missing rows are a representative random sample of all rows.

questions.text: You notice that high-income policyholders are more likely to leave the income field blank. What missing data mechanism is this?
options: MCAR — the missingness is random across all records
MAR — the missingness depends on a different observed variable
MNAR — the missingness depends on the missing value itself
Structural missingness — the field does not apply
questions.explanation: When the probability of a value being missing depends on the value itself (here, income), the mechanism is MNAR (Missing Not At Random). This is the most dangerous case because simple imputation will produce biased estimates.

questions.text: Why should you call prep() on the TRAINING set only, and not on the full dataset?
options: prep() is too slow to run on large datasets
Using the full dataset would cause data leakage — test set statistics would influence the imputer
recipes does not support full-dataset prep()
The test set does not contain missing values
questions.explanation: If you fit the imputer (e.g. compute the median) on the full dataset including the test set, information from the test set leaks into the training process. This gives an overly optimistic evaluation of model performance. Always fit transformers on the training set only.

questions.text: kNN imputation with k=5 replaces a missing value with:
options: The median of the entire column
The mean of the 5 nearest complete-case neighbours in feature space
A randomly drawn value from the observed distribution
Zero, unless the column mean is higher than the median
questions.explanation: kNN imputation finds the 5 records most similar (by Euclidean distance in the space of complete features) to the record with the missing value, then uses their mean as the imputed value. This preserves correlations between variables.

questions.text: Median imputation is an appropriate strategy for MNAR data, because the median is robust to outliers.
questions.explanation: Robustness to outliers is a desirable property, but it does not fix the MNAR problem. Under MNAR, the missing records are a biased (non-random) subset, so any imputed value derived from observed records will be systematically wrong. Robustness to outliers and correctness under MNAR are separate concerns.

options: Imputing missing values automatically
Visualising the pattern and proportion of missingness across columns
Testing whether missingness is MCAR using Little's test
Removing rows with any missing value
questions.explanation: vis_miss() draws a heatmap of missing vs. observed cells across all rows and columns, making it easy to see which columns are most affected and whether missingness co-occurs across columns. It is a diagnostic tool, not an imputation tool.
